speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Nonlinear scattering and a 2-adic logarithm example
summary: The first block on P000525 advertises Strauss's nonlinear scattering theory through comparison of a nonlinear flow with a simpler linear flow. Klein--Gordon and Korteweg--de Vries equations are examples, without a stated dimension, data class, or completeness theorem. The explicitly attributed Cartier example ``as presented by Gelfand'' occurs inside the ensuing discussion of \(p\)-adic measures on P000526 and is indexed here as an intervention, not a second uninterrupted talk. The archive's overlapping page ranges do not establish a different speaker for the unlabelled surrounding measure theory.

speaker: A. A. Kirillov
title: Metaplectic spinors and bounded p-adic measures
summary: After Gelfand's scattering announcement, Kirillov presents symplectic spinors through the metaplectic cover and the canonical commutation relations. The numbered second block treats \(p\)-adic measures, the bounded power-series transform, and the Newton--Mahler basis. Its speaker is not restated; assigning it to the continuing Kirillov block is an editorial reconstruction. The Cartier example explicitly credited to Gelfand is separated as item 1973-313.4. P000527 begins with the end of the Mahler argument before the new Fuchs heading.

speaker: D. B. Fuchs
title: The Q-construction and the Grothendieck group
summary: The continuation on P000527 gives Quillen's exact-category \(Q\)-construction and explains why its fundamental group is the Grothendieck group: objects determine loops and short exact sequences determine their additive relations. A separate line compares \(BQM\) with \(B\operatorname{GL}(\infty,A)\), omitting the loop-space shift. This material continues record 311, rather than introducing an independent K-theory construction.

speaker: A. A. Kirillov
title: Bundles associated with the metaplectic representation
summary: Kirillov resumes the symplectic-spinor discussion: local symplectic coordinates, lifted transition functions, and the Schwartz--Hilbert--tempered-distribution triple of associated bundles. A Heisenberg-algebra bundle is identified with \(TM\oplus\mathbb R\), but the accompanying degree bound for polynomials is one degree too large. Lagrangian planes are introduced at the end, before Schnirelman's heading.

speaker: A. I. Schnirelman
title: Fermi--Pasta--Ulam recurrence and a periodic-wave heuristic
summary: The talk reports numerical recurrence of energy initially placed in the first Fourier mode of a weakly nonlinear chain. Zakharov suggests approximation by an integrable differential system. The discussion passes to a string and to perturbations of the wave equation on the circle. Parameters, boundary conditions, numerical units, and the averaged first-order drift system are not fully recorded, so the numerical sketch and the asserted periodic drift cannot be promoted to general theorems.

speaker: D. B. Fuchs
title: The Lagrangian Grassmannian bundle
summary: A boxed intervention labels the space \(\Lambda\) of Lagrangian planes in \(\mathbb R^{2n}\) and the bundle \(RM\to M\). There is no further theorem, Maslov-class calculation, or quantization assertion in this block. It links Kirillov's notation on P000528 to the ensuing discussion without supplying an independent long talk.

speaker: A. S. Mishchenko
title: Fredholm representations and higher signatures
summary: Mishchenko defines a Fredholm representation, applies it to nonsingular Hermitian forms over a ring with involution, and constructs a signature by the difference of two Fredholm indices. The culmination is the characteristic-number formula for a closed oriented manifold. The exact constructions and formula were publicly announced in March--April 1973, from a submission received in October 1972. The fuller 1974 paper supplies proofs and a more general ring formulation. These are therefore expository E items, despite their close match to a later full publication.

speaker: V. A. Ponomarev
title: Free modular lattices, subspace representations and perfect elements
summary: Ponomarev passes from lattice identities to representations of the free modular lattice by finite families of subspaces. He defines perfect elements and gives recursive lattice words and a Boolean family generated by sums omitting one generator. These definitions and constructions match the 1974 Gelfand--Ponomarev paper. The separate conjecture that every modular lattice is a submodule lattice is false: the Arguesian condition is an older additional restriction. A question about classification must distinguish the tame four-subspace problem from the matrix-pair complexity already present for five subspaces.

speaker: S. I. Gelfand
title: Affine and spherical buildings
summary: After the end of Ponomarev's lattice discussion, S. I. Gelfand describes the Bruhat--Tits complex as a discrete analogue of a symmetric space. Maximal compact subgroups and Iwahori subgroups encode vertices and chambers. The rank-one picture is a tree; a finite-dimensional flag-incidence example over a finite field illustrates a spherical building. In source order this block precedes Kazhdan's curve-counting talk, although the archive numbers it later.

speaker: D. A. Kazhdan
title: The Stepanov--Bombieri method for counting points on curves
summary: Kazhdan explains a Riemann--Roch and Frobenius construction after Bombieri's June 1973 Bourbaki lecture on Stepanov's method. The notes omit the constant one in the projective Weil bound and compress two distinct multiplication maps into a single diagram. They also abbreviate the deduction of the full Weil estimate from a coarse upper bound, omitting the uniformity and covering argument emphasized by Bombieri. These are identifiable proof-compression defects, not new unsolved point-counting questions.

speaker: L. N. Vasserstein
title: Stable rank, Serre's problem and a conic reduction question
summary: The opening announcement reports a three-variable case of Serre's problem. Vasserstein then defines stable rank, connects the two-variable case to \(K_2(k)\), and exhibits the real degree obstruction. An incompletely defined winding symbol and symplectic \(K_1\) lead to a concrete conic question for polynomial, entire and continuous functions. The 1974 announcement matches both genuine results and an erroneous field dichotomy; the 1976 full paper separates the remaining field cases. The conic wording needs its coefficient field and the meaning of ``common divisor'' restored before it has a definite answer.

speaker: D. A. Kazhdan
title: Derived categories and total derived Hom
summary: Kazhdan develops the derived category from ordinary Ext: projective resolutions, comparison up to homotopy, complexes of maps, and localization at quasi-isomorphisms. He then describes total derived functors and their universal transformation. This is established Grothendieck--Verdier homological algebra, connected to the earlier 1971 derived-category discussions. The essential repairs are boundedness for the free-complex comparison theorem, variance for a contravariant functor, and the direction in which the universal transformation induces a map on natural transformations.
